Title: [Book][Response] Verify a selected seat is committed to the booking (visible on Retrieve, priced into the offer) as soon as Book succeeds, without waiting on any ticketing/payment step.
Capabilities / Test Data: TC-BOOK-POS-03's scenario (one AvailablePaid cellCode/cellId selected via passengersSelectedSeats), executed as a standalone Book -> Retrieve pair with no ticketing/payment trigger invoked in between.

Steps / Endpoint Chain: AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap (record cellCode/cellId) -> Book (submit passengersSelectedSeats) -> Retrieve immediately afterward, with no ticketing action taken in between -> inspect bookingStatus/ticketStatus alongside the seat-related fields.
Expected Result: Automatable assertion: the immediate post-Book Retrieve already shows passengersSelectedSeats/passengerSeats/totalSelectedSeatsAmount populated with the selected seat, while bookingStatus/ticketStatus still reads as un-ticketed/un-issued (e.g. Booked, not Ticketed). This confirms the seat is attached to the reservation at Book time and does not depend on a later payment/ticketing step existing or completing. If bookingStatus already reads as ticketed/paid immediately post-Book with no intervening action taken, record that as a finding rather than assuming the AC's ordering holds.
SpecReference: SPEC.md §2.9, §2.11; User Story AC5 ("allows the selected seat to be added to the booking before payment")
Notes: AC5 was the only acceptance criterion in the User Story with no test case explicitly mapped to it -- TC-BOOK-POS-03 confirms Book accepts and echoes a seat, and TC-RETRIEVE-REG-01 confirms a seat survives ticketing, but neither explicitly establishes that seat attachment happens at Book time, ahead of and independent from ticketing/payment. Note also that no distinct Payment endpoint exists anywhere in this collection/SPEC.md's scope -- "before payment" is interpreted here as "before ticketing/issuance", the closest later-stage checkpoint this API exposes; flag to the team if a literal payment-capture step exists outside this collection.
